articles.title: The Backup Business Nobody Talks About: What It Costs to Start One in 2026
articles.excerpt: Most IT people who want recurring revenue look at hosting, managed services or SaaS reselling. Very few look at backup - which is odd, because backup is the one service a small business cannot argue i…
articles.body: Most IT people who want recurring revenue look at hosting, managed services or SaaS reselling. Very few look at backup - which is odd, because backup is the one service a small business cannot argue its way out of once it has lost data. The numbers behind that demand are brutal. In 2026 just over half of ransomware attacks still managed to encrypt data, the median ransom demand reached US$769,000 and average recovery costs climbed to around US$1.7 million, according to Sophos' State of Ransomware 2026. Only about one in three smaller organisations stopped an attack before encryption. That is not a scare statistic, it is a market description. Millions of small companies run with no tested backup, no offsite copy and no idea what a restore would actually cost them.
articles.author: Tùng Xuân

articles.title: How to Keep Going When Motivation Disappears
articles.excerpt: How to Do Hard Things When You Have Zero Motivation There are days when you know exactly what you need to do. You need to study. But your brain says: “Not today.” The problem is that motivation doesn'…
articles.body: How to Do Hard Things When You Have Zero Motivation There are days when you know exactly what you need to do. You need to study. You need to finish the task. You need to fix the problem. You need to learn something new. But your brain says: “Not today.” The problem is that motivation doesn't always show up when you need it. So what do you do when motivation is at 0% ? Stop Waiting for Motivation One of the biggest mistakes we make is waiting until we feel motivated before taking action. But motivation often comes after action, not before it. Instead of asking: “How can I motivate myself to finish this?” Ask: “What is the smallest thing I can do right now?” That small action is often enough to get started. Make the First Step Ridiculously Small Don't try to finish everything at once.

articles.title: Optimizing Pull Request Reviews: Balancing Code Volume and Efficiency in AI-Assisted Development
articles.excerpt: Introduction The rise of AI-assisted development has unleashed a torrent of code, transforming the once-manageable pull request (PR) into a sprawling behemoth. What was once a few hundred lines, maybe…
articles.body: Introduction The rise of AI-assisted development has unleashed a torrent of code, transforming the once-manageable pull request (PR) into a sprawling behemoth. What was once a few hundred lines, maybe a thousand at most, now routinely balloons to 3200 lines or more , as developers leverage AI tools to generate code at unprecedented speeds. This explosion in code volume, while a testament to AI's power, is straining traditional review processes, raising critical questions about code quality, reviewer efficiency, and the very sustainability of software development in the AI era. Consider the cognitive load on a reviewer staring down a 3200-line PR. Cognitive load theory tells us that working memory has limits.

articles.body: Матрицу MITRE ATT&CK обычно ассоциируют с SOC, threat hunting и red team. Это база. Но она может быть полезна намного раньше — на этапе threat modeling, pentest, архитектурного review и CI/CD. И не только для инциденщиков, но и в теме Product Security. В статье разбираю, как перейти от isolated finding к attack path и связать attacker behavior с preventive controls, что такое security validation, причем тут runtime detection и release risk на примерах public API, SSRF → cloud, Kubernetes и software supply chain. Отдельно покажу, почему vulnerability нельзя автоматически превращать в ATT&CK technique и в каких Product Security сценариях ATT&CK лучше вообще не использовать.

articles.title: Attackers have been exploiting critical Zimbra flaw to steal emails
articles.excerpt: A simple email gives the attackers the ability to remotely inject OS commands.
articles.body: Hackers have been exploiting a critical vulnerability in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite in an attempt to obtain email backups and authentication credentials of vulnerable organzations, Microsoft has warned . The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-73570, lets attackers remotely issue operating system commands without authentication. Zimbra maintainer Synacor issued a patch on July 20, but didn’t disclose the vulnerability for more than three weeks after that. The security-focused Shadowserver Foundation said last week that its scans found that 274 separate instances of the Zimbra Collaboration Suite had been compromised. The number of servers running the software has fluctuated from 19,000 in the week following the patch to about 12,000 in the weeks following that.

The likes of Anaconda, Lake Placid, The Meg, and the granddaddy of them all, King Kong, offer a certain innate allure regardless of their differing quality, as they take a creature we might already find menacing and mega-plus-size them. Some lean into camp, some into pure horror, and some into tragedy, but a surprising number of them work on some level.
